Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators.

Automatic Execution Paths

  • pyproject.toml uses the uv_build build backend. In the provided text, there is no evidence of setup.py, .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, or malicious custom PEP 517 build-hook behavior that would cause arbitrary execution during installation.
  • [project.scripts] mon-tokenizer = "mon_tokenizer.cli:main" is a normal console_scripts entry point and requires the user to run the command. It is not evidence of automatic execution during installation or interpreter startup.
  • mon_tokenizer/__init__.py only imports MonTokenizer and defines metadata; no import-time credential theft, exfiltration, or persistence behavior is evident.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Obfuscation

  • No code was found that broadly searches environment variables, .env files, SSH keys, cloud credentials, CI/CD tokens, wallets, or kubeconfig files.
  • No evidence was found of archive creation, temporary staging, base64 packaging followed by upload, webhooks, external C2 endpoints, or raw-IP exfiltration.
  • No persistence mechanisms such as cron, systemd, launch agents, or shell profile modification were found.
  • No evidence of Kubernetes, Docker socket, cloud metadata, or GitHub Actions token-based lateral movement was found.
  • No obfuscated loader patterns such as eval/exec/compile, marshal/pickle loaders, compressed/encrypted staged payloads, or self-deleting droppers were identified.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • src/mon_tokenizer/data/mon_tokenizer.model was detected as a roughly 977KB binary/high-entropy file, but the README explicitly describes a bundled SentencePiece tokenizer model of that size, and the code loads that model. Based on the current evidence, it is not plausibly a hidden payload.
  • The runtime dependency twine>=6.1.0 in pyproject.toml may be somewhat unnecessary for a tokenizer library, but there is no accompanying evidence of credential theft or package-publishing token reuse.
  • The package version is 0.2.3, while __init__.py sets __version__ = "0.1.5". This appears to be a packaging/versioning inconsistency rather than evidence of malicious supply-chain compromise.
  • Within the provided material, there is no evidence of typosquatting, hidden native binaries, wheel/sdist mismatch, or sudden malicious dependency insertion.

Additional Verification Needed

  • The large binary model file (mon_tokenizer.model) was not fully validated from the text corpus alone. If needed, verify the SentencePiece model structure and compare hashes against the upstream source/release artifact.
  • This review is based on the provided extracted sdist text. If a wheel exists for the same version, compare the wheel and sdist for file and execution-path differences.
